evals.prompt: Turn this pasted Power BI insight into a requirement without MCP or a ticket adapter.
evals.expected_output: Works the pasted path end to end: clarifies user, problem, outcome, scope and open questions first, then drafts the local story and the canonical local work item. Never treats the missing MCP server or adapter as a blocker (`requirements tasks blocked on MCP availability = 0`), and attempts no external sync — there is no declared adapter to emit prepare_story through.

evals.prompt: Use a verified read-only MCP server to turn Excel analysis into acceptance criteria.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the server and its visible read tools first — a configuration file alone does not prove availability — then cites the connected source in the story context and follows the identical local workflow. Requests no write access to read analysis, and derives every criterion from the supplied analysis (`acceptance criteria invented from missing business context = 0`).

evals.prompt: The MCP server is unavailable. Continue the BA/PO task.
evals.expected_output: Records the warning and switches to the pasted/manual input path without pausing the work: MCP availability is never a blocker for local requirements work. The story and local work item are produced exactly as on the verified-MCP path, minus the cited source.

evals.prompt: Resolve this existing external ticket through the configured adapter.
evals.expected_output: Routes to story-intake and uses only the adapter declared in `.agentic/guides/project.md` (`provider-specific API calls made outside the declared adapter = 0`). Normalizes the lookup receipt and reads the ticket's title, body, and acceptance criteria back before treating any of it as requirements.

evals.prompt: The approved story should be synced through the configured adapter.
evals.expected_output: Runs the workflow in order: canonical local work item first, then the provider-agnostic prepare_story intent through the declared adapter, then normalizes the receipt into the schema-1 shape and reads the ticket back to verify title, body, and acceptance criteria against what was approved. A success receipt alone is a claim, not evidence (`adapter syncs recorded as successful without a read-back verification = 0`); the receipt and history entry are recorded either way.

evals.prompt: The configured adapter fails during story sync.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the approved local story and work item authoritative and does not discard or roll them back (`local stories discarded on adapter failure = 0`). Records the failed receipt with its warning and a matching local history entry, claims no read-back it never performed, and offers retry plus a manual fallback — handoff is not blocked by the failure.

Asks focused questions on user, problem, desired outcome, and scope before drafting anything — step 1 precedes the story, and no adapter is invoked. Gaps the business has not answered stay in the open-questions list rather than becoming plausible-sounding criteria (`acceptance criteria invented from missing business context = 0`).

evals.prompt: Create the external ticket now without showing me the payload.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: approval given without the payload in view is not approval, so the write cannot proceed (`external tickets created or updated before explicit approval = 0`). Presents the step-4 review — story, acceptance criteria, open questions, complete ticket payload — and waits. Passing 'the story above' as the payload instead is equally refused (`adapter payloads passed as conversation-only references = 0`).

Installs the ba-po preset alone: dispatcher routing, the operating-model and MCP-onboarding guides, and the intake/story-author skills — and no developer, QA, architect, or delivery assets. A role-only install carries no code-writing agents and no git-hook layer, so the scaffolded governance promises no gate it does not install.

evals.prompt: Add a developer role to the existing BA/PO installation.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs additively against the recorded install journal: the preset union becomes ba-po + developer, shared IDs resolve to the one already-journaled asset rather than a second copy, and user-edited files are never rewritten. Every BA/PO asset survives, and the registry gains the developer rows without duplicating the dispatcher row — one source of truth per asset.
